title: An integral morphism to a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme is a limit of finite morphisms
statement:
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and $
u:Y	o S$ an integral morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Then there are a directed set $I$, an inverse system of $S$-schemes $(
u_i:Y_i	o S)_{i\in I}$ with transition morphisms $t_{i'i}:Y_{i'}	o Y_i$ ($i'\ge i$) over $S$, and morphisms $p_i:Y	o Y_i$ over $S$ with $t_{i'i}\circ p_{i'}=p_i$, such that every $
u_i$ is finite and of finite presentation, every $t_{i'i}$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism] (indeed finite), and $(Y,(p_i)_i)$ is a limit of the system in the category of schemes. (Concretely: $
u_*\mathcal O_Y$ is the filtered colimit of finite and finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-algebras $\mathcal A_i$, Properties 0817, and $Y_i=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S(\mathcal A_i)$.)
